tasks.short: Select, store, order, issue and inventory classroom supplies.

steps.what: Check classroom equipment, materials and supplies that are short.
Read stock and open orders for those classroom supplies.
Select which classroom materials and supplies to order.
Draft the order for the selected classroom supplies.
Accept the classroom order for equipment, materials and supplies.
Send the accepted classroom order to purchasing.
Store delivered classroom equipment and supplies in the cupboard.
Issue classroom materials and supplies to the students.
Count the classroom inventory still held in the cupboard.

tasks.design: The teacher still checks the cupboard, selects what to order, stores deliveries, issues materials and counts the classroom inventory. {PROCUREMENT} shows on-hand stock and open orders, and the requisition is the lines they marked, so the separate order form and the chasing e-mail drop. The head of department still accepts that requisition before it is sent to purchasing.
tasks.previous_blocker: The cupboard list sat on a sheet apart from purchasing, so every order was typed again.
tasks.enabler_now: The purchasing system can show stock and raise a requisition from marked lines. No model is required.
tasks.still_hard: Catalogue codes differ by supplier, and a delivery rarely matches the order. The teacher still selects, stores, issues and counts.
tasks.human_edge: Judging what this class actually needs, and whether a delivered item is fit to store and issue.

ambition.what: Reorder a classroom supply while it is under par, before the cupboard is empty.

tasks.altitude: The teacher still selects, stores, issues and counts. They no longer retype the order or chase it by mail. The head of department still decides whether it is sent.

reach.task: Place the accepted classroom order with the supplier
reach.learn: Which equipment, materials and supplies the teacher selected and the head of department accepted.

evidence.claim: A purchasing system that already stores items and requisitions can show on-hand stock and raise a requisition from marked lines. That is configuration, not a model.
A classroom order that names no pupil is ordinary internal purchasing data. A line that identifies a pupil's personal aid is personal data and needs the school's existing basis.

assumptions: The school already has a purchasing system with items, on-hand quantity, par, catalogue code, cupboard and requisition status. The teacher or the office maintains the codes.
The teacher marks lines to order. The requisition is those lines. An amount over the department limit waits for the head of department.
Pupil names are not on the stock list. Upkeep of codes and par quantities is about one hour per 100 hours of this task.
unknowns: Whether this school's purchasing system can show cupboard stock, or only orders.
Who may accept a classroom requisition, and the amount that needs a second person.
Whether classroom stock is the teacher's job or the office's.
research_questions: Can the current purchasing system raise a requisition from a stock line without a separate sheet?
What is the approval limit for a classroom order in this department?

already_counted.description: Checking shortages, storing deliveries, issuing materials and counting the cupboard still take the teacher's time.

incremental.description: Update catalogue codes and par quantities when the supplier or the room changes.

approvals.approved_version: Classroom order for the selected equipment, materials and supplies this month, as the head of department accepted. A later change voids the acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A month of classroom orders where the stock view and the requisition replace the sheet and the e-mail. Selecting, storing, issuing and counting stay. If half the lines have no catalogue code, the teacher still types those and the saving is the low end.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Library help, hall and cafeteria watch, and bus duty.

steps.what: Rewrite the duty rota for the school library and cafeteria.
Read which administrative duties fall this week.
Give school library assistance while students are there.
Keep monitoring the hall and the cafeteria.
Supervise bus loading and unloading at the school.

tasks.design: The teacher still gives library assistance, monitors the hall and the cafeteria, and supervises bus loading and unloading. The weekly duty rota is entered once on {CALENDAR}, so the paper copy drops. No model watches the duty or infers how students feel.
tasks.previous_blocker: The timetable and the duty list sat apart, so the teacher recopied the week onto a slip.
tasks.enabler_now: A calendar the school already has can hold each duty once.
tasks.still_hard: A missing colleague, a swapped slot, and students at the bus still need a person there. A model must not watch or score the duty.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a student who is unsafe in the library, the hall, the cafeteria or at the bus, and acting then.

ambition.what: Ask for a duty swap the day before when the rota shows two gaps on the same bus.

tasks.altitude: The teacher still stands the library, hall, cafeteria and bus duties. They stop copying the rota onto a slip.

reach.learn: Which library, hall, cafeteria and bus duties this teacher stood, and which were swapped.

evidence.claim: A shared calendar can hold a weekly duty once, so a paper copy of the same rota is unnecessary.
Staff consent applies to a tool that can monitor them.

assumptions: The duty rota fields are teacher, day and slot: library, hall, cafeteria or bus. The deputy head publishes it. The teacher reads it.
The calendar does not track location and does not score the teacher. No pupil names are on the rota.
Checking a swapped duty is about 0.4 hours per 100 hours of this task. There is no model cost.
unknowns: Who publishes the rota today, and whether bus duty belongs to this teacher.
Whether the school calendar already has a duty view the teacher can read.
research_questions: Does the current calendar already hold the duty rota, or is it still a separate sheet?

already_counted.description: Reading the duty and standing library, hall, cafeteria and bus duties still take the teacher's time.

incremental.description: Check a swapped duty on the calendar when the rota changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A term of duties where the paper copy of the rota drops and the teacher still stands each slot. A week of swaps, where they still confirm the change in person, sits at the low end.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher still chooses classroom supplies, stores and issues them, and still stands library, hall, cafeteria and bus duties. Retyped orders and recopied rotas drop. The head of department still accepts a classroom order before it is sent.
reach: The purchasing officer places the accepted classroom order and needs the selected lines, not a second sheet.
The deputy head publishes the duty rota and needs to see which library, hall, cafeteria and bus duties this teacher stood.
skills_to_grow: Mark a stock line instead of retyping a classroom order.
Read the duty from the calendar rather than a paper slip.
Stay with students on the duty, and do not hand that watch to a model.
role.ambitious_version: Each cupboard shows its par, and a short line is on the requisition before the month's order closes. The duty rota is visible the week before. The teacher still selects, issues and stands the duty in person.
